title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)

steps.what: Fetched the ten HCPortal records and 18 original scans of HStAM 4 h 1411 through api.hcportal.eu.
Harvested all 176 HCPortal cipher-key records of the Marburg key volumes with their users; no Malsburg key. Keys 5 (Sixtinus 1635), 30, 38 and 49 compared with f. 3.
f. 3 transcribed by hand from 2x line crops (455 groups).
Homophonic annealing of f. 3 alone against de-1640s, with and without a letter-frequency penalty.
Remaining pages transcribed by two agents in the same format (about 9,000 more groups); ff. 30-31 found to duplicate ff. 28-29.
Annealing ff. 3+12+18 (1,575 groups): all four restarts converged on the same key and German text (das ich auch noch nit weiss ... garnisonen ... contributiones vom platten lande).
Letter signs valued from context: N/D ch, Y/G ei, Z/O st, W/P ss, L/A tt, R/C/E/M mm, X/j/J sch, H ll, S/F au, T/B ff, Q ai; single figures are numerals.
Digit table re-annealed and polished over all pages with the signs fixed: 23, 40, 75 corrected; rare groups 14, 17, 20, 33, 85 assigned.
Dictionary-segmentation measure; the same measure on shuffled keys gives 50-58%.
236 unread groups re-checked against the scans: 24 misreads and 2 doubled groups corrected, 210 confirmed as written.
Codes valued from context: 128 Cöln, 130 Hamburg, 188 die Staaten, 253 Regiment, 273 Compagnien (grade I).
f. 12 letter-cipher block: many-to-one and null-allowing annealing in German, Latin, French, Italian and Dutch; periodic IC for periods 1-15; Caesar shifts; HCPortal letter keys 2 and 105.
Web search for an edition of the Malsburg letters (Rommel, LAGIS); none found.
Reading measured: 9,338 of 9,736 cipher tokens in words (95.9%); 193 code/sign tokens open; 97.9% of the non-code text.

Integrated Larry Beck with ChatGPT's separate alphabetic investigation, preserving Bourdeau's original numerical work and provisional alphabetic input. The supplied revised edition and audit were inspected; this is an integration date, not a claimed first-discovery date.

Compared the preserved ten original lines with the selected image-reading branch and uncertainty apparatus. Legacy 531 raw letters include eight editorial-label letters, giving 523 ordinary cipher positions; the selected branch has 510. Separate model reading passes and six binary source choices remain explicitly qualified.

Reproduced the contributed decryption with alphabet abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz, repeating subtraction 4,5,3,6,2, phase 0 and continuous line handling. Special labels are outside the stream. Re-encryption is only a consistency check; the public verifier does not independently authenticate source readings or historical identities.

Integrated the ten-line literal output separately from editorial German and English. Retained tqouppen, itzigdn, the er ... wurden anomaly, blot and source alternatives. Conditional opening and possible proposed-letter scope prevent treating dismissal, payment or troop movements as accomplished facts. No coherent-text percentage is asserted.

Integrated inspected documentary findings and their limits: Geyso p.99 n.2 paraphrases an uninspected Malsburg letter of 16 November 1636 concerning Melander and authority; retention letters complicate an actual-dismissal hypothesis. Koblenz 47/4400 is a catalogue lead for cipher codes, not an inspected matching key. No values for 43, 45 or LL established.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 9506 tokens, 119 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.066 per letter; random keys -5.639 (z 15.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.662 (mean -3.692, z 52.7); annealer on the real text -2.423. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per-record transcriptions ct/hcp*.txt and the folio files f0*.txt; decryption reading_segmented.txt (measured text, one block per folio) and work/reading_auto.txt for the address leaves; the alphabetic block from Larry Beck's alphabetic/ package; keys key.txt, codes.txt and the alphabetic key in alphabetic_reading.md.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): reading_segmented.txt read letter by letter and the alphabetic block's edition. ff. 12-13, 18, 23-24, 25 and the alphabetic block build German sentences with codes as name holes (kept read, reviewed B); ff. 3, 14, 15-17, 28-29 (and its duplicate 30-31) and 32-33 have open codes, bracketed letters or noise in most sentences, relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.959 (tokens in dictionary words) -> 0.436.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.073; polyphony 0.0; 230 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.423

outcome.method_basis: Bourdeau recovered the numerical table by ciphertext-only annealing; the separate Beck/ChatGPT contribution recovered the alphabetic repeating shifts from the provisional ciphertext, with subsequent image-reading corrections and no external plaintext crib.

parts.label: The numerical cipher in the ten letters (ff. 3-33), Bourdeau
parts.basis: Bourdeau's original numerical measure: 9,338 of 9,736 cipher tokens in words (95.9%); duplicate ff.30-31 excluded; alphabetic block excluded. Original numerical first-break claim retained as reported.

parts.label: Separate alphabetic block at the foot of digital image 0012, Beck with ChatGPT
parts.basis: Five-shift alphabetic mechanism recovered; 523 normalized original positions and 510 in selected image-reading branch. Substantial continuous German with source alternatives and unresolved forms; three labels in five occurrences unidentified. No measured coherent-text percentage or independently established first-break priority.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: tokens of the documents that read as sentences (profile documents, duplicate HCPortal 508 excluded): 497 (712) + the alphabetic block (510) + 504 (639) + 505 (2,015) + 506 (592) = 4,468 of 10,246; 496, 502, 503, 507 and 509 are decoded, not read. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.959 = measure.py over reading_segmented.txt, 9,736 cipher tokens of the numerical letters, a token read when all its letters fall in dictionary words; 193 open code/sign tokens unread; alphabetic block excluded.

gaps.item: about 40 numerical three-digit codes and name signs (193 tokens)
gaps.detail: Bourdeau's numerical scope: about 45 groups in total, five contextually valued (grade I). These counts are not combined with the separate alphabetic code vocabulary.

gaps.item: alphabetic 43, 45 and LL: three labels, five occurrences
gaps.detail: No primary code equation or named parallel; no shared nomenclature established. Koblenz 47/4400 contents uninspected.

gaps.item: alphabetic source alternatives in lines 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, plus blot
gaps.detail: Selected 510-position branch and bounded alternatives retained; original or better authentic imaging plus human hand comparison needed to settle strokes and blot extent.

gaps.item: alphabetic tqouppen, itzigdn and er ... wurden
gaps.detail: The alphabetic mechanism is recovered, but no independent primary parallel or fair copy is available to establish the intended forms. Literal output and conjectures remain separate; physical access has not been shown necessary.
[E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative; clearer authentic imaging or same-hand comparison is needed before expansion.
No contemporary attribution or matching named parallel established. Original correspondence and a possible Hoff comparison remain uninspected; physical access has not been shown necessary.

outcome.notes: Numerical work and its original measured result remain credited to Daniel Bourdeau. Alphabetic contribution by Larry Beck with ChatGPT; separate AI passes are not human paleographic validation. Overall fraction and code totals are unknown because the distinct systems are not combined. Original numerical first-break status was reported true; priority of the contributed alphabetic result was not independently established. Melander is a documentary lead, not an identified code. Full alphabetic key behavior is recovered, while code values and source readings keep the overall key and text partial. fraction_read, codes_open and first_break are the numerical cipher's original measured values, restored on merge; the alphabetic block is carried in parts.

credits.note: PR #17: period-five key of the f. 12 alphabetic block recovered (with ChatGPT), critical reading

texts.label: ff. 3-4, 5/15 Jan 1637
texts.note: reading_segmented.txt f003: an open three-digit code or a bracketed single letter every few words (<201>, <239>, <+>, <193>, <f>, <210>, <4#>, <144>) and broken word division ("reg arn [i] sonen"); holes in most sentences
texts.summary: Malsburg reports that he does not know where the garrisons' upkeep is to come from now that the contributions from the open country have ended, and urges that a safe-conduct for the envoys to the peace talks at <128 Cöln> be solicited from the King of Hungary. Block 'work/f003.txt' of reading_segmented.txt; f. 4 (address leaf) only in work/reading_auto.txt.

texts.label: ff. 12-13, Wesel, 7/17 Jan 1637

reading_review.note: reading_segmented.txt f012-f013: once the broken word division is closed up the German builds sentences (ich weis nun nicht, wie ich den Weg anstellen [soll] ... ob ich alleine zu ... soll erst erwarten, dan durch Friesslant mitt Wagen und Pferden zugehen ist unmoglich) with open codes as name holes, about one per sentence.

texts.summary: From Wesel: he does not know whether to go to <148> or to the army; the recruits and Dalwig's Verehrungsgelder, Eberstein's regiment, and the impossibility of travelling through Friesland with wagons and horses; word that it was decided at Regensburg to give the envoys to <128 Cöln> no safe-conduct, and of talks apart at <130 Hamburg> or Lübeck. Block 'work/f012.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

texts.label: f. 12 foot, the alphabetic block of 7/17 Jan 1637 (Larry Beck with ChatGPT)

reading_review.note: alphabetic/alphabetic_reading.md: the selected literal output of the ten-line block reads as continuous German (Der [43] stehet itzo aufm Sprunge ... sie mit den Schwedischen Generalen des Commendo halber sich nicht uergleichen wurden) with an editorial German and English; holes are the code labels 43, 45, LL and two residual forms.

texts.summary: A separate ten-line block in a letter cipher with repeating shifts 4, 5, 3, 6, 2, deciphered by Larry Beck with ChatGPT; the selected reading discusses command, the Swedish generals, the reciprocal joining of forces and the authority requested. A working edition: the code labels 43, 45 and LL are unidentified.

texts.label: f. 14, Jan 1637
texts.note: reading_segmented.txt f014: open codes, <?> and bracketed letters in nearly every clause ("dar anni tuer hind | <?> | [r] lich"); holes in most sentences
texts.summary: The provisioning of Hermannstein (Ehrenbreitstein); Obrist Hoffman's troops; marches by Marburg, Corbach and Brilon on the road from <128 Cöln>; Jan de Werth at Cologne. Block 'work/f014.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

texts.label: ff. 15-17, Jan 1637
texts.note: reading_segmented.txt f015-f017: f015 is fragments between codes; f016 has <120>, <129>, <193>, <212> and bracketed letters in most sentences; holes in most sentences
texts.summary: No audience yet; notice of the end of the Stillstand; companies and dragoons, with recruiting patents already issued; the ambassador of <188 die Staaten>; money and horses. Blocks 'work/f015.txt' and 'work/f016.txt' of reading_segmented.txt; f. 17 only in work/reading_auto.txt.

texts.label: f. 18, 14/24 Feb 1637

reading_review.note: reading_segmented.txt f018: the frozen and crippled cavalry, the dead, the new recruits, the obligation for the Hermanstein journey; builds sentences with broken word division and a few codes.

texts.summary: Some of the <212> are so frozen that several have become cripples; the obligation over the loss before Hermannstein; the new recruiters. Block 'work/f018.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

texts.label: ff. 23-24, 7/17 Feb 1637

reading_review.note: reading_segmented.txt f023-f024: f023 reads as continuous argument (the dispute whether Hermanstein was effectivement provisioned, the Felshaber's bond, paying the carters and freeing the prisoners); f024 has more codes but its sentences build (a separate peace with the imperial commissaries; how to leave French service without harm).

texts.summary: The dispute over whether Hermannstein was effectively provisioned; ransom and gifts for the commanders; the finding that 'we have dealt with a Frenchman'; peace talks in Picardy with nobody sent to <128>; a separate peace with the imperial commissioners; the garrisons ruined. Blocks 'work/f023.txt' and 'work/f024.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

texts.label: f. 25, 5 Mar / 23 Feb 1637

reading_review.note: reading_segmented.txt f025: [120] resolved to content the carters, but not the costs for the prisoners; his brother; his private affairs. Codes and broken division, but the sentences build.

texts.summary: <120> has resolved to content the Reuter; ransom for prisoners; letters of exchange. Block 'work/f025.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

texts.label: ff. 28-29, 28 Mar 1637 (old style)
texts.note: reading_segmented.txt f028-f029: codes, COMPAGNIEN/REGIMENT groups and bracketed letters in most clauses ("| 7 | <193> | <212> | stuck | <197> |"); only the route passages of f029 build; holes in most sentences
texts.summary: The journey by the Watten; twelve-pound cannon and constables; Jan de Werth between Ruhr and <268>; the States' alliance and a muster place in Cleves; the conjunction at Cloppenburg, Quakenbrück, Minden, Vechta, Wildeshausen and Diepholz. Blocks 'work/f028.txt' and 'work/f029.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

texts.label: ff. 30-31, 'Duplicat' of ff. 28-29
texts.note: duplicate of ff. 28-29 (excluded from the measure); its decode is as holed as theirs
texts.summary: The duplicate of the 28 March letter, re-copied with different line breaks; used only as a check copy and not deciphered or counted separately, so its text is that of HCPortal 507 (blocks 'work/f028.txt' and 'work/f029.txt').

texts.label: ff. 32-33, 3 Apr 1637 and Mar 1637
texts.note: reading_segmented.txt f032-f033: largely noise ("den ream bas sad rex tra ordin", "sel zame dinge umb") with a code group every few words; holes in most sentences
texts.summary: A French letter signed '232' of 3 Apr 1637, citing a letter of the ambassador extraordinary in London, and German news extracts from London of 16/26 Mar in a second hand, in the same key; paired large capitals are name signs. Blocks 'work/f032.txt' and 'work/f033.txt' of reading_segmented.txt.

prior.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

human: Original numerical work: Bourdeau posed /goal from catalogue entry 338, suggesting the 1635-52 key sheets; no target-specific intervention recorded. Later alphabetic contribution: Larry Beck directed a separate ChatGPT investigation, supplied research goals and requested source and computational checks. ChatGPT performed computation, separate image readings and drafting. This is an external contribution, not part of the original Claude session; exact contributor model IDs, first-discovery date and session count are unknown.
